newsitem.title: UK: Bradys barely stir in the wait for U.S. rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Bradys barely stir in the wait for U.S. rate rise.

text.p: Emerging market debt hardly budged on Friday, overwhelmed by increasing speculation that next week will finally see a rise in U.S. interest rates.
"There's going to be an increase...possibly once the decision has been made our market will stabilise and then strengthen," one European bank trader said.
However, there was a danger than if U.S. rates go up by only 1/4 of a point, speculation of another imminent rise will continue to keep pressure on emerging debt, he added.
Traders said a 25 basis point increase is largely priced into Bradys which have been stuck in a very narrow range for most of the past two weeks.
"A small U.S. rate hike will not detract from improving fundamental reasons for future bullishness, so we expect increased volumes after the FOMC," ANZ analyst Jerome Booth said.
He pointed to fresh interest in Russia after the sweeping changes in the cabinet which have brought reformist Anatoly Chubais in as economic supremo.
A planned national strike for March 27 is not causing too much concern at the moment and Booth expected it to have limited support.
However, one trader said it was making him more cautious about the outlook for Russian debt over the rest of this month.
